From c589e3ca27c9f608004b155d3acb2fab6f7a9f26 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Palmer Dabbelt <palmer@rivosinc.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Sep 2022 10:09:00 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] RISC-V: Avoid coupling the T-Head CMOs and Zicbom

We could make the T-Head CMOs depend on a new-enough assembler to have
Zicbom, but it's not strictly necessary because the T-Head CMOs
circumvent the assembler.

Fixes: 8f7e001e0325 ("RISC-V: Clean up the Zicbom block size probing")
Reported-by: kernel test robot <lkp@intel.com>
Reported-by: Conor Dooley <conor.dooley@microchip.com>
Signed-off-by: Palmer Dabbelt <palmer@rivosinc.com>
Reviewed-by: Heiko Stuebner <heiko@sntech.de>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220915170900.22685-1-palmer@rivosinc.com
Signed-off-by: Palmer Dabbelt <palmer@rivosinc.com>

diff --git a/arch/riscv/include/asm/cacheflush.h b/arch/riscv/include/asm/cacheflush.h
index a89c005b4bbf..273ece6b622f 100644
--- a/arch/riscv/include/asm/cacheflush.h
+++ b/arch/riscv/include/asm/cacheflush.h
@@ -42,8 +42,12 @@ void flush_icache_mm(struct mm_struct *mm, bool local);
 
 #endif /* CONFIG_SMP */
 
-#ifdef CONFIG_RISCV_ISA_ZICBOM
+/*
+ * The T-Head CMO errata internally probe the CBOM block size, but otherwise
+ * don't depend on Zicbom.
+ */
 extern unsigned int riscv_cbom_block_size;
+#ifdef CONFIG_RISCV_ISA_ZICBOM
 void riscv_init_cbom_blocksize(void);
 #else
 static inline void riscv_init_cbom_blocksize(void) { }
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/riscv/include/asm/cacheflush.h`**
   - A comment block was added to clarify the relationship between the T-Head CMO errata and the Zicbom ISA. The comment states that the T-Head CMOs internally probe the CBOM block size but do not depend on Zicbom.
   - The `#ifdef CONFIG_RISCV_ISA_ZICBOM` preprocessor directive was retained, but the associated function `riscv_init_cbom_blocksize` is now conditionally defined. If Zicbom is not configured, a static inline function that does nothing is provided instead.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications establish a clearer separation between the T-Head CMOs and the Zicbom ISA. By adding the comment, the patch clarifies that while the T-Head CMOs can probe the CBOM block size, they do not require Zicbom to function. This change reduces unnecessary coupling between the two components, allowing for more flexibility in the use of the T-Head CMOs without being dependent on the Zicbom configuration.

Here is the commit message:
RISC-V: Avoid coupling the T-Head CMOs and Zicbom

We could make the T-Head CMOs depend on a new-enough assembler to have
Zicbom, but it's not strictly necessary because the T-Head CMOs
circumvent the assembler.

Fixes: 8f7e001e0325 ("RISC-V: Clean up the Zicbom block size probing")
Reported-by: kernel test robot <lkp@intel.com>
Reported-by: Conor Dooley <conor.dooley@microchip.com>
Signed-off-by: Palmer Dabbelt <palmer@rivosinc.com>
Reviewed-by: Heiko Stuebner <heiko@sntech.de>

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220915170900.22685-1-palmer@rivosinc.com
Signed-off-by: Palmer Dabbelt <palmer@rivosinc.com>

Here is the root cause:
The T-Head CMOs were incorrectly coupled with the Zicbom ISA, leading to unnecessary dependencies that could cause issues if the assembler was not new enough to support Zicbom. This coupling was not required since the T-Head CMOs can function independently by probing the CBOM block size internally.

Reason:
The T-Head CMOs were incorrectly dependent on the Zicbom ISA, which created unnecessary coupling. This meant that if the assembler was not new enough to support Zicbom, it could lead to issues when initializing the CBOM block size, as the T-Head CMOs could function independently without this dependency.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
/*
 * The T-Head CMO errata internally probe the CBOM block size, but otherwise

 */
```
Reason:
The comment clarifies that the T-Head CMOs can probe the CBOM block size internally and do not require the Zicbom ISA, thus removing the unnecessary dependency and preventing potential issues with older assemblers. This change ensures that the T-Head CMOs operate correctly without relying on the Zicbom configuration.
